title: The Appointment from Selfority
author: Selfority
description:
Only 66% of middle-aged women have discussed menopause with their healthcare provider. Why? Most spend 15 minutes or less in the exam room, and many go in unprepared to articulate their symptoms or advocate for their care.

The Appointment from Selfority® replaces confusion with clarity.

Each episode is a conversation between the Selfority co-founders focused on a single question. Seasoned executive Rachelle Kuramoto sits in the role of the patient, and Dr. Sarah Berg answers, bringing over a decade of clinical experience as an OBGYN and Menopause Society Certified Practitioner.

This is a place for medically grounded answers and the calm that comes with knowing what’s happening is normal. You'll get information and resources, along with compassion (and a touch of humor).

The Appointment is for informational and educational purposes only. It's not medical advice. Please work with your healthcare provider to make decisions that are right for you.

title: Cycle Sisters Podcast: Navigating the IVF Sea

description: Welcome to the Cycle Sisters Podcast! Join us as we navigate the stormy, often lonely sea of IVF. We realized the vital power of connection, so together we share our experiences and honest opinions for anyone even thinking about IVF or already in the depths of it. The IVF road can often be long and arduous, full of unpredictable ups and downs, but you don't have to weather it alone. Sail along with the Cycle Sisters and let's navigate these uncharted waters together.

title: The Soft Life & The Real Life
author: Victoria Mumbi njue
description:
🌸 The Soft Life & The Real Life

The Soft Life & The Real Life is a podcast for women, by women — a safe space for honest conversations about the beautiful, complicated, and sometimes messy journey of being a woman.

We talk about femininity, relationships, love, money, self-care, confidence, ambition, motherhood, friendships, healing, independence, and personal growth — without pretending that life is always perfect.

Because behind the “soft life” are real women navigating real responsibilities, challenges, dreams, disappointments, and victories.

Whether you're building your career, raising a family, finding yourself, healing from heartbreak, chasing your dreams, or simply trying to enjoy life, there is a place for you here.

Expect real stories, deep conversations, laughter, lessons, different perspectives, and topics women often discuss privately but rarely say out loud.

From Africa to the rest of the world, The Soft Life & The Real Life celebrates women in all their different seasons and reminds us that there is no single way to be a woman.

Because you can be soft and strong.
You can be ambitious and feminine.
You can have dreams and still have difficult days.
You can want the soft life while being honest about the real life.

🌷 The Soft Life & The Real Life — real women, real conversations, real life.

Our lessons are designed to help you understand not only what Portuguese speakers say, but also how and when to use the language naturally. You can learn useful expressions for introducing yourself, asking questions, shopping, traveling, ordering food, talking about your daily routine, making friends, and handling everyday conversations. We also explore common mistakes, pronunciation tips, essential vocabulary, and simple explanations that make Portuguese easier to understand and remember. Our goal is to make learning Portuguese enjoyable and accessible. Instead of memorizing endless rules, you’ll gradually develop your listening and speaking skills through practical examples and meaningful repetition. Whether you're learning Portuguese for travel, work, study, relationships, or personal growth, you'll find lessons to help you progress step by step. 🎧 Listen carefully.

title: Marriage Counseling with Paul Zohav | Tucson, AZ
author: Paul Zohav
description:
Welcome to Marriage Counseling with Paul Zohav — the podcast for couples who want to build stronger, more honest, and more lasting relationships.

Paul Zohav M.Ed. is a licensed marriage and communication counselor based in Tucson, Arizona, with over 30 years of experience helping couples navigate the most challenging moments in their marriages. He holds a Master's degree in Counseling from the University of Virginia and is the author of Marriage and Communication: Recipes for Life — a practical guide to communication skills for couples at every stage of their relationship.

In each episode, Paul shares the real tools, frameworks, and insights he uses every day in his counseling practice in Tucson, AZ. Whether you are newlyweds building your foundation, a couple working through conflict and communication breakdowns, partners recovering from infidelity and trying to rebuild trust, empty nesters rediscovering each other, or someone preparing for marriage through premarital counseling — this podcast is for you.

Topics covered include:

  • Marriage counseling and couples therapy
  • Communication skills for couples
  • How to rebuild trust after infidelity and cheating
  • Premarital counseling and preparing for marriage
  • Relationship counseling and conflict resolution
  • Couples counseling in Tucson, Arizona
  • Online marriage counseling via Zoom
  • Family communication and parenting
  • The five love languages and personality types in relationships
  • How to apologize and restore broken trust
  • Body language and nonverbal communication in marriage
  • Moving from reacting to responding in difficult conversations

Paul works with couples in person in Tucson, AZ and online via Zoom with couples across the United States. His approach is practical, warm, and grounded in over three decades of real counseling experience.

If you and your partner are struggling with communication, navigating infidelity, preparing for marriage, or simply want to build a deeper and more connected relationship, Paul Zohav is here to help.

title: Up North Uncut
author: Jonny Hillhouse
description:
Up North Uncut is about life in the remote Far North of Australia’s east coast — Cape York — the people, the places and the stories that deserve to be remembered.


Hosted by Johnny and Cody, we get into pig hunting, fishing, camping, Cape York adventures and the wild shit that happens along the way. From chasing big boars through the scrub and big barra in the creeks, to sitting down with the legends we’ve met over the years and the characters we’re yet to meet.


But more than anything, it’s about capturing the stories, yarns and memories that too often get told around a campfire, have a few laughs, and then disappear with time. We want to record them, share them and make sure some of those stories don’t get lost.

No polished bullshit. Just good yarns, good people and a look at life Up North — past, present and whatever comes next.


This is Up North Uncut.

description:
Home is more than a place. It’s where who we are shapes how we love, lead, connect, and grow.

Anchored at Home is a podcast with husband-and-wife duo Josh and Liz Nolz about doing the deeper work within ourselves so we can show up differently in the relationships and lives that matter most.

Through honest conversations about marriage, family, emotional health, faith, identity, and personal growth, Liz and Josh explore what it means to build a life that feels grounded from the inside out. Drawing from their work as coaches—and, just as importantly, their own experiences of marriage, parenting, healing, and growth—they bring both perspectives to the table: the practical and the personal, the head and the heart.

This isn’t a space for quick fixes or pretending to have it all figured out. It’s a place to slow down, get curious about what’s happening beneath the surface, and have the conversations that can lead to greater connection, wholeness, and lasting change.

title: Maths for Kids / Maths is Not Boring: The Kids Maths Podcast
author: Kidopoly
description:
A groundbreaking podcast for curious kids aged 4-12 that proves maths is anything but dull.

Join our fictional AI hosts Mira, a brilliant 9-year-old, and her younger brother Finn, age 7, as they set off on a journey into one great mathematical idea each episode. From numbers that never end and shapes with only one side to the strange rules of chance and the secret patterns in a snowflake, each episode uncovers an idea that is simple at its heart and extraordinary because it is everywhere - told in a way that actually makes sense to kids.

Nobody does sums here. Whether you're discovering why infinity comes in different sizes, how a shuffled pack of cards is almost certainly in an order no one has ever seen, why honeycombs are made of hexagons, where the number zero came from, or what makes a prime number special - Maths is Not Boring turns big ideas into stories that ignite curiosity and wonder, and gives kids one more clue to how the world works.

Because maths isn't a list of rules to learn. It's the most beautiful way anyone has ever found of seeing the world.


A note on why we use AI. For us, AI allows us to deliver learning at a scale and quality that previously would have been too expensive. If we make the odd technical error, or the sound goes a bit funny, bear with us, we’re trying our best. We hope you enjoy the show!

title: Kitchen management
author: trixie tacla
description:
🎙️ Podcast Script: Kitchen Management

Title: “Behind the Kitchen: The Importance of Kitchen Management”


Hello everyone, and welcome to our podcast!

Have you ever wondered why some kitchens seem organized, clean, and stress-free, while others can become messy and chaotic?

The answer often comes down to one important thing: kitchen management.

In today's episode, we're going to talk about what kitchen management is, why it is important, and how proper management can make food preparation safer, easier, and more efficient.

So, let's get started!

🎵 MUSIC FADES OUT


---

PART 1: What is Kitchen Management?

HOST:

First, what exactly is kitchen management?

Kitchen management is the process of organizing, planning, and controlling the different activities in a kitchen. It includes managing ingredients, equipment, time, cleanliness, food preparation, and the people working in the kitchen.

In simple words, kitchen management means making sure everything and everyone in the kitchen is properly organized and working efficiently.

For Cookery students, learning kitchen management is important because it helps us develop skills that we can use not only in school but also at home and in future workplaces.


---

PART 2: Why is Kitchen Management Important?

HOST:

So, why is kitchen management important?

There are several reasons.

First is efficiency.

When a kitchen is properly organized, we can find ingredients, tools, and equipment more easily. This saves time and makes food preparation smoother.

Second is food safety.

Proper kitchen management helps prevent food contamination. Keeping ingredients separated, cleaning equipment, washing hands, and storing food properly are all important practices for keeping food safe.

Third is cleanliness and sanitation.

A clean kitchen is more pleasant to work in and helps reduce the risk of contamination. Cleaning work surfaces, washing utensils, and properly disposing of waste are important parts of kitchen management.

And finally, kitchen management helps promote teamwork and responsibility.

When everyone knows their assigned task, the work becomes more organized and productive.


---

PART 3: Important Areas of Kitchen Management

HOST:

Now let's talk about some important areas of kitchen management.

1. Time Management

Time is very important in the kitchen.

Before starting to cook, it is helpful to plan the steps and determine which tasks should be done first. This prevents unnecessary delays and helps ensure that food is prepared on time.

2. Proper Use of Equipment

Kitchen equipment should be used correctly and safely.

Before using equipment, we should know its purpose and proper operation. After using it, it should be cleaned and stored properly.

Taking care of equipment also helps make it last longer.

3. Ingredient Management

Ingredients should be properly checked, prepared, stored, and used.

We should pay attention to food quality and expiration dates. Proper storage can help maintain food quality and reduce unnecessary food waste.

4. Kitchen Cleanliness

Cleanliness should be maintained before, during, and after cooking.

This includes washing hands, cleaning work surfaces, washing utensils, and keeping the kitchen organized.

Remember: clean as you go.

This simple habit can make a big difference.


---

PART 4: Kitchen Management as a Cookery Student

HOST:

As Cookery students, we may sometimes think that kitchen management is only important for professional chefs.

But that's not true.

Every time we prepare food for a practical activity, we are already practicing kitchen management.

For example, before cooking, we can prepare all the ingredients and equipment we need.

During cooking, we can keep our workspace clean and organized.

After cooking, we can properly clean and store the equipment and dispose of waste.

These small practices help us become more responsible and disciplined in the kitchen.


---

PART 5: Practical Tips

HOST:

Here are five simple tips that every Cookery student can remember:

Number one: Plan before you start.

Know your recipe, ingredients, equipment, and procedures.

Number two: Keep your workspace organized.

Put things where they belong and avoid unnecessary clutter.

Number three: Practice proper food safety.

Wash your hands, prevent cross-contamination, and store food properly.

Number four: Clean as you go.

Don't wait until everything is finished before cleaning.

And number five: Work as a team.

Good communication and cooperation can make kitchen activities much easier.

And that's all for today's episode of “Behind the Kitchen.”

We've learned that kitchen management is more than simply keeping a kitchen clean. It involves planning, organizing, managing time and resources, practicing food safety, using equipment properly, and working responsibly with others.


Remember: A well-managed kitchen creates a better cooking experience.

Thank you for listening, and see you on our next episode!

title: How to make cake,icing,decorate a cake
author: Trina Tacla
description:
‎Hello and good day, everyone! Welcome to my podcast. I’m your student host Trina Tacla, and for today’s episode, I’m going to share with you one of the skills I learned in Cookery, which is how to make a cake, prepare icing, and decorate it.
‎
‎The title of my podcast is "HOW TO MAKE A CAKE, ICING, AND DECORATE A CAKE"
‎
‎For me, baking is an interesting skill because it allows us to be creative while learning how to properly prepare food. It may look simple, but we need to be careful with the measurements and follow each step correctly.
‎
‎Okay, now let me introduce the ingredients that we will need.
‎
‎Ingredients for the Cake
‎
‎for the Batter:
‎
‎- 1¼ cup cake flour
‎- ¼ cup evaporated milk
‎- ¼ cup oil
‎- ½ cup white sugar
‎- ½ tsp salt
‎- 1 tbsp baking powder
‎- 2 tbsp vanilla
‎- 4 pcs egg
‎
‎Meringue:
‎
‎- 4 egg whites
‎- ¼ cup white sugar
‎- 1 pinch cream of tartar (C.O.T.)
‎
‎Icing:
‎
‎- 1 egg white
‎- 100 g unsalted butter
‎- 150 g powdered sugar
‎- 200 g lard
‎- 1 tsp vanilla
‎
‎Now that we have all our ingredients ready, let’s start making the cake.
‎
‎Procedure for the Batter
‎
‎First, separate the egg yolks from the egg whites. Set aside the egg whites because we will use them later for the meringue.
‎
‎For the batter, mix the egg yolks and white sugar. Then, add the evaporated milk, oil, and vanilla and mix them well.
‎
‎In a separate bowl, combine the cake flour, baking powder, and salt. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet mixture and mix until well combined.
‎
Procedure for the Meringue
‎
‎Next, let’s prepare the meringue.
‎
‎Put the 4 egg whites in a clean bowl and beat them until foamy. Add the cream of tartar, then gradually add the white sugar.
‎
‎Continue beating until the meringue becomes fluffy and forms stiff peaks.
‎
‎Gently fold the meringue into the cake batter. After that, pour the batter into a prepared cake pan and bake until fully cooked.
‎
‎Once the cake is done, let it cool completely before adding the icing.
‎
‎Procedure for the Icing
‎
‎Okay, now let’s move on to the icing.
‎
‎First, beat the unsalted butter and lard until smooth. Gradually add the powdered sugar while mixing.
‎
‎Then, add the egg white and vanilla. Continue mixing until the icing becomes smooth and creamy.
‎
‎Decorating the Cake
‎
‎Now that the cake and icing are ready, it’s time to decorate the cake.
‎
‎First, spread the icing evenly on the top and sides of the cooled cake.
‎
‎Then, use a piping bag to create simple designs such as borders, flowers, or other decorations.
‎
‎For me, decorating the cake is one of the most enjoyable parts because I can use my creativity and improve my skills.
‎
‎Through this experience, I learned that baking requires proper measurements, patience, cleanliness, and practice. I also learned that mistakes are part of learning, and we can improve by practicing more.
‎
‎And that’s all for today’s episode of “From Batter to Cake.”
‎
‎Thank you so much for listening to my podcast. I hope you learned something from my simple baking experience.
‎
‎Once again, I’m your student host Trina Tacla. Keep practicing, keep learning, and enjoy baking!
‎
‎Thank you for listening, and goodbye!
‎

Most people never find out what they're capable of. This show is for the ones who refuse to die wondering.
I'm Sinan. From addiction and trouble with the law to multiple businesses, seven kids, and a mission to help people become unstoppable.
Real talk on business, mindset, and faith. The strategies that grow real income and the inner game that keeps you steady. No fluff, no fake gurus, just the truth.

title: SCARS AND ALL
author: SCARS & ALL
description:
We all have scars. Some people hide them well, others don't, but the truth is, no one is exempt. We live in a world that only shows the finished product, the nice car, the good job, the happy family, and never the struggle it took to get there.


Scars and All is a podcast about that struggle, told honestly. Host Frank Wills sits down with a wide range of guests, people in recovery, families who've supported a loved one through it, doctors, lawyers, nurses, clinicians, and everyone in between, who have failed, sometimes more than once, and found the courage to try again. No filters. No muting. Just the real story behind the struggle, the pain, and the comeback.

If you're in early recovery, staying sober one day at a time, supporting someone you love through it, or just wondering how you ended up in the same place again, this show is for you. Recovery is possible. You can still become who you were meant to be, and it starts with getting honest.

New episodes released weekly.

title: Cooked & Curious
author: Stanton Davidson
description:
*Cooked & Curious*
is a podcast about strange stories, wild theories, unexplained mysteries, forgotten history, and the questions that make you stop and say, “Wait… what?”
We’ll dig into everything from conspiracies and bizarre historical events to the genuinely unexplained, taking a look at the stories, the evidence, the stupidity, and everything in between. I’m not here to tell you what to believe—and I sure as hell don’t always have the answer. I’m here to follow the rabbit into the hole, figure out what holds up, and see where we end up.
Expect some actual research, plenty of questionable decisions, laughter, and probably a few moments where I realize I might be completely wrong.
So grab a drink, get comfortable, and come get cooked with me.
*Stay curious. Question everything.*
*And remember: I could be wrong.*
email us here at - open@cookedandcuriouspod.com

Each episode picks up where the weekend message leaves off, because there's always more to say than a weekend allows, and gets practical about living it out in your home and relationships. author: Tawhid
description:
Rise Again is a motivational podcast for anyone going through a difficult season in life.

When life knocks you down, it can feel like there is no way forward. But sometimes, all you need is one more reason to keep going.

Rise Again shares powerful motivational stories, inspiring life lessons, comeback journeys, and mindset-changing conversations designed to help you rebuild your confidence, find your strength, and keep moving forward.

Whether you are facing failure, disappointment, financial struggles, loneliness, or simply feel stuck in life,

You may fall.
You may struggle.
You may feel lost.

But you can always Rise Again.

🎙️ Rise Again — Fall Down. Get Back Up. Rise Again.

title: Charmed
author: iHeart Australia
description:
Hosted by Sam Todd, Charmed is a podcast about collecting, nostalgia, pop culture and the personal stories behind the things we treasure.
Warm, funny and a little bit obsessed, Charmed celebrates the emotional pull of the small stuff - the lucky charms, sentimental jewellery, childhood souvenirs, irrational purchases and tiny treasures that somehow become part of who we are.
Ever kept a concert ticket for years? Held onto a charm because it reminds you of someone? Refused to part with a childhood toy, a Disney pin, a friendship bracelet or a tiny piece of merch that means way more than it probably should?
That’s where Charmed begins: with Sam stepping inside the worlds of collecting, nostalgia and personal obsession to uncover the stories behind the things people keep close.
Each episode explores a different collecting world - from Disney and fashion archives to fandom, pop culture, toys and accessories - and Sam isn’t doing it alone. She’s joined by familiar faces from each of these worlds, unpacking the pieces they treasure most and the memories tucked inside them.
It’s whimsical, nostalgic in all the right ways, and made for anyone who knows the smallest things can hold the biggest stories.
Because sometimes we collect things. And sometimes, what we’re really collecting are memories.
Follow Sam at @samtodd

title: Future Plates
author: AfriFOODlinks
description:
Future Plates explores the future of food in Africa’s rapidly growing cities, asking a simple but urgent question: as Africa urbanises, what will we be eating?


Across four episodes, the series looks beyond what is on our plates to the people, places, cultures and systems that determine how food reaches us and how it affects our lives.


The series unpacks why good nutrition matters in the first 1,000 days of life, the value of local food traditions and knowledge passed between generations and why informal markets are important places of both trade and nourishment for millions across the continent. We also look at city governance mechanisms to understand how policy, planning, infrastructure and public services can help build healthier and more equitable food systems.


At a time when Africa is experiencing the fastest urban growth in the world, the choices being made today will shape cities and food systems for generations to come. Future Plates brings together lived experiences and diverse voices of experts, practitioners, food systems actors, city officials, youth, academics and civil society to examine the challenges, opportunities and choices that will determine what Africa’s urban food future looks like..


Future Plates is an ARC production in partnership with AfriFOODlinks – a project funded by the European Union.


Visit the AfriFOODlinks website for more information about the project: https://afrifoodlinks.org/

title: Why Having a Good Job Made Me Feel Like a Failure
author: Maleeka Hollaway, Life and Business Success Coach
description:
Episode 1: Why Having a Good Job Made Me Feel Like a Failure
What happens when your life is actually going well, but it doesn't look like the version of success you once had?
I have a good job. I enjoy what I do. I'm paid well. And somehow, having a job still made me feel like I had failed.
In this first episode of Success, Dismantled, I'm unpacking the realization that the job was never really the problem. The problem was what it represented: I wasn't where I used to be, and I was still measuring my life against an old definition of success.
We're talking entrepreneurship, identity, achievement, career transitions, starting over, and what happens when who you are now no longer fits the scorecard you've been using.
Maybe you're not failing. Maybe your definition of success just hasn't caught up with who you've become.

description:
A true story of crime, corruption and two impossible thefts.


In 1965 the world’s largest uncut diamond is stolen from the Natural History Museum, the man arrested is David Knight, a 24 year old window cleaner who lived just yards away. 


Now Josie Long tells his extraordinary story. There was no evidence placing David at the scene, and the police officers who claimed he confessed were far from squeaky clean. 


But if he was innocent when he went into prison, he certainly wasn’t on his release. After he walks out of Wormwood Scrubs he embarks on an audacious life of crime, culminating in a famous heist that only a handful of people in the world knew he was responsible for…until now.

You don’t need another crash diet before your next trip, Pride weekend, or beach vacation.

Operation Speedo is a 16-week coaching program built for gay men 40+ who want to build a body they feel confident in—and learn how to actually maintain it.

Inside this video, Steven explains the three-part approach we use with our clients:

Build the muscle and shape you want with intentional progressive training.
Track your nutrition long enough to understand what your body actually needs.
Sustain your results without living in the gym, tracking every bite forever, or starting over before every vacation.

Steven is a 48-year-old certified personal trainer who has been coaching since 2003 and has helped more than 600 gay men work toward their health, fitness, and body-composition goals.

This isn’t about getting in shape for one weekend.

It’s about getting there—and knowing how to stay there.

Host Joseph Lewin knows it too—the tightness in his chest at dinner, the brain that won't switch off on a weekend when the pipeline's dry.

title: Who Told You You Can't Have Both?
author: Alyssa Wolff
description:
Who told you you couldn’t have both?


You wanted the business AND the kids.


The money. The ambition. The work that lights up your brain. The family vacations, the hobbies, the random Tuesday afternoon where nobody needs anything from you.


Somewhere along the way, you were handed a pretty crappy choice.


Be ambitious, but accept that your business will take over.

Be present with your kids, but accept that your business will have to come second.

Want more money, but accept that you'll have less time.


I don't buy it.


You can have the business. You can have the kids. You can have the ambition, the money, the clients you love, and a life that actually has room for all of it.


You just can't keep managing every single thing required to make all of that happen.


That's what we're getting at inside this private podcast.


I'll show you the lies I keep seeing entrepreneur moms get sucked into when they’re capable enough to make almost anything work… but secretly sick of being the person everything ELSE in their life depends on.


We'll talk about the hidden third job, the responsibilities that somehow become permanent, why the goal-crushing projects keep getting pushed to next week, and why getting better at managing everything (and everyone) is never the answer.


And as you listen, I want you to notice your own week.


What's taking over? What's getting bumped? What's still landing on your plate just because you're good at handling it?


When something in this podcast makes you think, “Oh... that's happening in my business too,” that's your cue.

You don't have to figure it all out yourself.


That's what the Business Cleanout is for.


You hand me the whole ridiculous pile. The business, the team, the projects, the responsibilities, the things you've somehow become responsible for remembering.


I'll help you figure out what stays, what goes, what needs to move, and what needs to stop being yours.


Because you wanted business AND kids…. You just can't keep carrying everything required to have both.


So let's figure out what’s going to make both possible.


→ Take a look at the Business Cleanout

These are the calls being made in real time, by the people making them. Each session is an honest account, where we explore beyond the superficial, not a highlight reel. What would I do if this were my shop?

Alongside solo breakdowns, we bring on top operators and experts each week to give you clarity across the areas that impact your business and life most:

Personal finance and wealth building
Retirement planning for business owners
Technology and operational efficiency
Lending, capital, and growth strategies
Tax strategy that actually moves the needle

You will learn:
How to read your numbers like an operator, not a bookkeeper
Where profit is leaking and how to fix it fast

What top-performing shop owners do differently

Whether you are an established shop owner or an aspiring operator looking to make the leap, this podcast will give you the financial clarity and perspective you need before making your next move.

If you are tired of guessing, reacting, and hoping your numbers work out, this is for you.

Because the shops that win are not the busiest.

They are the ones who understand what is under the hood.

description:
The Soul of a Woman Speaks is a faith-filled Christian podcast for women navigating grief, loss, heartbreak, widowhood, life transitions, emotional healing, and the journey of starting over.


Hosted by Dr. Patricia Shaw, Christian Life and Relationship Coach, author, speaker, and widow, this podcast creates a safe space for honest conversations about what happens when life changes without warning—and how you learn to breathe again when the life you knew no longer exists.


Through raw personal stories, biblical encouragement, prayer, practical life lessons, and heartfelt conversations, Dr. Patricia shares her journey of loving deeply, losing unexpectedly, grieving honestly, and discovering that there is still purpose after pain, joy after sorrow, and life after loss.


Each episode explores topics such as healing after the death of a spouse, Christian grief support, finding yourself after loss, overcoming heartbreak, rebuilding your life, trusting God through grief, emotional healing for women, faith during difficult seasons, identity after loss, forgiveness, relationships, self-discovery, and finding purpose after tragedy.


This is more than a podcast about grief. It is about what happens next.

It is for the woman who has been broken but knows she is not finished.
The woman learning how to live again.
The woman rediscovering her faith, her voice, her identity, and her purpose.
The woman who is ready to Break. Bloom. Become.

If you are learning how to breathe again after love, loss, heartbreak, disappointment, or life-changing pain, you are in the right place.

Come as you are. Bring your questions, your tears, your faith, and even the pieces you haven't figured out yet.


Because sometimes healing begins when the soul of a woman finally speaks.

title: Sin Vergüenza by Somos
author: Somos
description:
There’s no shortage of rules for how a Latina is supposed to live. Be ambitious, pero no te pases. Make your family proud, but don’t take up too much space. Work hard, but don’t make anyone uncomfortable by wanting more. And if you dare to question any of it? Well, you might just be called una sinvergüenza.


For generations, that word has been used to shame us into silence and keep us in our so-called place. But what if being a sinvergüenza isn’t an insult? What if it’s where you find your freedom?

title: Birthday Wishes in Marathi – Heartfelt Marathi Birthday Messages
author: Birthday
description:
Welcome to Birthday Wishes in Marathi, a podcast dedicated to beautiful, heartfelt, and meaningful birthday wishes in the Marathi language.

Birthdays are special moments that give us an opportunity to celebrate the people we love and appreciate. A simple birthday message can bring a smile to someone's face, make them feel remembered, and create a beautiful memory. But sometimes, finding the right words can be difficult. This podcast is created to help you discover the perfect birthday wishes for every special person and every special relationship in your life.

At https://birthdaywishinmarathi.org/, we explore a wide variety of Marathi birthday wishes, messages, greetings, quotes, and ideas that you can easily share with your loved ones. Whether you are looking for a sweet message for your mother or father, a loving wish for your husband or wife, a special message for your brother or sister, or a fun birthday greeting for your best friend, you will find inspiration here.

Our episodes cover different types of birthday messages, including emotional birthday wishes, romantic birthday wishes, funny birthday messages, short WhatsApp birthday wishes, traditional Marathi greetings, heartfelt wishes, and inspirational birthday quotes. We also explore birthday wishes for children, parents, grandparents, teachers, relatives, colleagues, and other important people in your life.

Marathi is a beautiful language that allows emotions and feelings to be expressed in a warm and personal way. Sending a birthday wish in Marathi can make your greeting feel more connected and meaningful, especially when the recipient understands and loves the language.

Each episode is designed to give you simple and useful ideas that you can use for birthday cards, WhatsApp messages, social media posts, text messages, or personal greetings. Whether you want something short and simple or a longer emotional message, our podcast aims to help you find words that truly express your feelings.

Along with our podcast, you can explore BirthdayWishInMarathi.org for more Marathi birthday wishes and messages organized around different relationships, occasions, and styles. Our goal is to make it easier for you to find the right words whenever someone special in your life has a birthday.

So, if you love sharing meaningful birthday wishes in Marathi, make Birthday Wishes in Marathi part of your celebration. Listen to our episodes, discover new messages, and share your favorite wishes with the people who matter most to you.

Thank you for listening and joining us. We hope our Marathi birthday wishes help you make every birthday a little more joyful, personal, and memorable.

For more beautiful Marathi birthday wishes, visit BirthdayWishInMarathi.org.

Celebrate birthdays. Share happiness. Express your feelings with words from the heart.

Happy Birthday and best wishes for a wonderful year ahead!

title: The Identity Edge with Lucy Cronly and Anne Marie Beggs
author: Anne Marie Beggs and Lucy Cronly
description:
The Identity Edge

What can a pair of shoes, a garden, a dance floor, a paintbrush or a

suitcase tell you about who you are?

Quite a lot, as it turns out.

Welcome to The Identity Edge, a podcast with Lucy Cronly and Anne-

Marie Beggs, where we take everyday things we love fashion,

gardening, travelling, dancing, painting, creativity, singing and even

choosing the right shoes and look at them from a slightly different angle.

The best way to understand ourselves isn't to sit down and ask, “Who

am I?”

It could be:

“Why did I choose those shoes?”

“What am I growing in my garden?”

“Why am I afraid to dance?”

“Whose picture am I trying to paint?”

“Where am I actually going?”

Or even most importantly…

“Is this still the life I want to be wearing?”

Were interested in the stories hiding underneath the everyday choices

we make.

Things we try or avoid or we think we're “not good at.”

Things we did once and stopped doing or even the things we've always

wanted to do but somehow never quite got around to.

Creativity isn't just about being creative.

Gardening isn't just about gardening.

Fashion isn't just about what you wear.


Travel isn't just about where you go and singing isn't necessarily about

having a good voice!

They're all opportunities to notice ourselves our values, our beliefs, our

confidence, our fears, our curiosity, our assumptions and the choices we

make when nobody is telling us what we should do.

That's where The Identity Edge comes in.

We;re going to have some fun along the way. There will be stories,

ex'eriments, probably a few questionable artistic efforts, and the

occasional moment when one of us says, “I am not doing that!”

Underneath the fun is something quite serious, that self-awareness

matters.

When we take the time to understand ourselves better, we can make

choices more consciously and live with greater intention.

We don't believe you need to become a completely different person.

Quite the opposite we want to explore what happens when you get

curious about the person who's already there, your own unique self.

Whether you're standing in front of your wardrobe, digging in the garden,

booking a flight, picking up a paintbrush, stepping onto a dance floor or

wondering whether you still fit the life you've created...come and explore

with us.

This is The Identity Edge.

We believe finding yourself starts with something as simple as choosing

the right shoes.

A podcast about Spiritual awakening, consciousness, and what it actually means to wake up inside your own life.

I'm Tom and with my partner Cheri, we've spent nearly a decade living and traveling in an RV. The deeper journey didn't start on the road — but the road is where we finally slowed down enough to hear it.


Every week we sit down with people whose lives were changed by something they couldn't explain — near-death experiences, spiritual awakenings, and the quiet shifts that happen when an ordinary life quietly stops being enough.


Together we explore:

• Consciousness 

• Inner peace 

• Life purpose 

• Intuition 

• The afterlife 

• The questions most of us only ask in the dark


No hype. No jargon. No asking you to believe anything you can't feel for yourself.


THE ROAD IS A SPIRITUAL PATH


Because so much of our own awakening happened on wheels, one thread runs through every conversation. Nature, solitude, letting go of the house and the stuff and the schedule. It turns out the RV was never really the point — getting out there was simply how we got quiet enough to hear what was already there.


Awakening isn't about leaving your life behind. It's about finally being awake inside the one you already have.


If you've felt the pull toward something more — after a loss, a close call, or in the silence of a long drive — you're in the right place.

The Robot Bureau is a monthly podcast on physical AI, humanoid robots and the Chinese companies building them, made for business leaders in Europe who need to understand what is coming before it arrives.


It is hosted by two people who have spent their careers as mirror images of each other. Rogier is a European founder who built and sold companies in China over 15 years. Lei is a Chinese founder who has spent 15 years building businesses in Europe. Between them they read the Chinese sources, sit in the Shenzhen showrooms and the European boardrooms, and translate what each side gets wrong about the other.


Every episode follows the same format. We pick the biggest headlines of the month, from Unitree and AgiBot to Bosch and Schaeffler, from a $6 billion funding round to a robot factory opening in Serbia, and then go beyond the headline to find the real story. We pitch those stories to each other, argue about what they mean, and end every episode with a verdict: which story makes the front page, which one is a nothing burger, and which one gets spiked.


We have all seen the demo videos, the kung fu moves and the robot Olympics. This show is about what is actually happening behind them: who is shipping, who is buying, who is on the bill of materials, and what it means if you run a business in Europe.


Reporting from Europe and China. New episodes every month.

title: Angielski na luzie. Projekt Ósmoklasista
author: Kinga Zabłocka
description:
Na hasło "egzamin ósmoklasisty" czujesz dreszcze, a wizja majowych arkuszy spędza Ci sen z powiek? Spokojnie, ogarniemy to!

"Angielski na luzie" to Twój bezstresowy przewodnik po egzaminie z języka angielskiego. Zamiast wkuwać wszystko na miesiąc przed, ruszamy z przygotowaniami we wrześniu. Małymi krokami, bez paniki i bez zarywania nocy budujemy formę, która w maju pozwoli Ci napisać arkusz na maksa.
W krótkich, 10-15 minutowych odcinkach rozkładamy egzamin CKE na czynniki pierwsze. Tłumaczę znienawidzone czasy gramatyczne bez nudnych regułek, demaskuję największe pułapki (tzw. dystraktory) i sprzedaję sprawdzone triki na darmowe punkty z e-maila.
Czego możesz się spodziewać?
Zero owijania w bawełnę: Skupiamy się tylko na tym, co realnie pojawia się na testach.
Strategii i lifehacków: Jak strzelać w lukach, gdy nie znasz słowa, i jak słuchać, żeby usłyszeć odpowiedź.
Materiałów bonusowych: Do odcinków dorzucam estetyczne, konkretne ściągawki w PDF, checklisty i mapy myśli do pobrania, które od razu możesz powiesić nad biurkiem.
Podcast to maraton, a nie sprint – startujemy od podstaw i powoli wchodzimy na wyższe obroty, żeby na wiosnę szlifować same detale. Zaparz ulubioną herbatę, załóż słuchawki i przekonaj się, że angielski da się lubić.

Zaobserwuj, żeby nie przegapić żadnego odcinka. A jeśli szukasz więcej szybkich tipów, quizów i edukacyjnych kulis, wpadnij na Facebook'a:

https://www.facebook.com/profi...

Tam oprócz dodatkowych zadań do samodzielnego ćwiczenia będę wrzucać więcej porad!

title: The unofficial Alton Towers podcast
author: Unofficial Alton Towers
description:
The Unofficial Alton Towers Podcast

Alton Towers has been drawing visitors to the Staffordshire moorlands for over two hundred years — first as a private estate and gardens, then as one of Europe's most significant theme parks. It has given the world the first suspended looping coaster in Europe, one of the most famous inverted coasters ever built, and a catalogue of closed attractions that fans still argue about decades later.

It has also given the world four-hour queues, baffling car park charges and a fast-track system that costs more than the ticket.

This podcast covers both sides honestly.

What each episode covers

We alternate between deep dives and practical guides. Deep dives look at individual rides, the lore behind the theming, the engineering decisions, and the attractions that no longer exist. Practical episodes tackle the questions visitors actually ask — how to structure a day, when the park is genuinely quieter, whether an on-site hotel stay pays for itself, and how to avoid the traps that cost families hundreds of pounds a year.

Who it's for

Coaster enthusiasts who want the detail. Parents planning a first visit who don't want to waste money. Anyone who's been going since childhood and wants to know what happened to the rides they remember.

Why independent matters

Official channels have a job to do, and that job is selling tickets. Ours isn't. When a ride is running one train, we say so. When a package is poor value, we say so. When the park gets something right — and it frequently does — we say that too, and we mean it.

The Unofficial Alton Towers Podcast is produced by the team behind unofficialaltontowers.co.uk, an independent visitor guide and fan site.

The Unofficial Alton Towers Podcast and unofficialaltontowers.co.uk are not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to Alton Towers Resort or Merlin Entertainments. All views are our own.
